chunks: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (rh) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from his father. He said: Abu Ahmad Muhammad b. Ziyad al-Azdi narrated to us. He said: I heard Malik b. Anas the jurist of Medina say:

I would visit al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (as), and he would give me a pillow, show me esteem, and say: 'O Malik, indeed I love you.' I would be delighted by that and praise Allah for it. He was a man never free from three qualities: either fasting, standing in prayer, or remembering Allah. He was from the greatest worshippers and the greatest ascetics who were in awe of Allah. He would speak much hadith, his gatherings were pleasant, and he was of much benefit. Whenever he said 'the Messenger of Allah (s) said', his colour would turn green at one time and pale another, until one who knew him would not recognize him. I performed Hajj with him one year. When his ride was prepared at the Ihram, every time he intended to recite the talbiyya, his voice cut off in his throat, and he almost fell from his ride. So I said: 'Say it, O son of the Messenger of Allah, and you must say it.' So he said: 'O Ibn Abi Amir! How can I dare say "I am at Your service, O Allah, I am at Your service" while I fear that He may reply to me: "I am not here for you, nor for your pleasure!"'

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةِ: the talbiyya; the ritual proclamation of readiness during Hajj that begins with 'Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk'
key_terms.الزُّهَّادِ: the ascetics; those who renounce worldly attachment in favour of devotion to Allah
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ: I am at Your service, O Allah, I am at Your service; the Hajj pilgrim's response to Allah's call, expressing total submission

ai.seo_question: How did Malik b. Anas describe Imam al-Sadiq's worship and God-consciousness during Hajj?
ai.summary: Malik b. Anas, the renowned Sunni jurist of Medina, gives a firsthand account of Imam al-Sadiq's (AS) character. He describes the Imam's hospitality and personal affection toward him, then enumerates three qualities the Imam was never without: fasting, standing in prayer, or remembering Allah. He ranks the Imam among the greatest worshippers and ascetics, noting his abundant knowledge and pleasant company. Malik describes how the Imam's colour would change dramatically when quoting the Prophet (S). Most strikingly, during Hajj the Imam could barely pronounce the talbiyya out of overwhelming awe, fearing that Allah might reject his response -- revealing the depth of his God-consciousness that surpassed all outward piety.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa`d Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from his father. He said: Abu Ahmad Muhammad b. Ziyad al-Azdi narrated to us. He said: I heard Malik b. Anas the jurist of Medina say:

I would visit al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as), and he would give me a pillow, exalt me, and say: O Malik, surely, I love you. I would become happy with that and praise Allah for it. He (as) was always upon three conditions: either he was fasting, standing in prayer, or remembering Allah. He was from the greatest worshipers and the greatest ascetics who were in awe of Allah. He would speak much, his gatherings were good, and he was of much benefit. Whenever he would say “the Messenger of Allah (s) said”, his colour would change from blue to pale, to the extent that one who knew him would deny him [because of how different he looked]. I performed Hajj with him one year. When I prepared his ride at the Sanctuary, he recited the talbiyya until he lost his voice and almost fell off his ride. So, I said: “Say it, O son of the Messenger of Allah, but not in that way.” So, he said: “O Ibn Abi `Amer! How can I dare say ‘I am at Your service, O Allah, I am at Your service!’ while I fear that He may reply to me with ‘I am not here for you, nor for your pleasure?!’”
